assembly_rules: R1: screen_kind != 'poker_table' => state is null regardless of every other answer. No table recommendations for non-table screens.
R2: Any board or hero card slot unreadable, or the pot not visible, or (seated) to_call/hero_chips not visible => evidence.readable=false and state null. Never fabricate a value or default.

R3: hero cards (p1): a slot is 'absent' only when rank AND suit are confidently no_card; a card only when both are confident card values; anything else is unreadable. Both absent with action_on_hero false => hero_cards []. A mix => state null.

R4: board (p2): slot k is absent iff rank_k and suit_k are both confidently no_card, a card iff both are confident card values (T => '10' rank 'T'; suits map s/h/d/c), else unreadable. Take slots in order until the first absent; every later slot must be absent; the count must be 0, 3, 4 or 5; any unreadable => state null. The street is DERIVED by core-engine::table_rules::Street::from_board_count (0 preflop, 3 flop, 4 turn, 5 river/showdown).

R5: amounts (glyph passes): the server segments the crop into n <= 8 glyphs (overflow => not visible; n = 0 => nothing displayed => not visible). Every g1..gn must be a confident character (any low confidence or not_a_character => not visible). The text must match ^(\d{1,3}(,\d{3})+|\d+)(\.\d{1,2})?$; ',' is stripped; value = round(decimal x 100) as u32 (hundredths). Not visible => R2.

R6: available_actions = the act_* questions answered yes. Assembly must NOT repair inconsistencies (e.g. to_call 0 with fold offered): if the set is inconsistent with the unchanged validator's rules, evidence.readable=false and state null. The validator is the gate. The assembled envelope is checked with the unchanged parse_screen_output before it is returned; any failure returns the same screen_kind and evidence with readable=false and state null (degrade, never repair).
R7: min_raise_to/max_raise_to: not visible => null (optional fields), but if raise is offered and either bound is not visible => state null (R2).

R8: players array (tier 2): Hero first (hero_seat_index), then SeatN for present seats in fixed clockwise order. last_action 'none_visible' => null. A present seat with not-visible chips => state null when action_required.
R9: hero_position is an envelope extension consumed by the decision layer only; it never relaxes envelope validation. Its value is DERIVED per R11; the hero_position answer is a cross-check.
R10: tier 0+1 without tier 2 may produce observations but never an actionable state (action_required must be false when seat data is absent).
R11: position: dealer_button_seat is not asked in 0.4.0 (not answerable from a 512 px tile and no seated captures exist), so hero_position is always null/unknown. Restored when seated captures exist.

R12: street cross-check (sheet p.3-5): game_phase must equal the derived street, except that five board cards accept river or showdown and game_phase chooses between them. Any other disagreement => state null (the inconsistency the first Gemma baseline showed: preflop declared with four board cards).

R13: actions (sheet p.3-4, p.9): preflop options are fold/call/raise; postflop the first player may check or bet and later players fold/call/raise; all-in is always an action. 'bet' is reported through act_raise and assembled as 'raise'. Consistency is enforced by the unchanged validator (to_call 0 => check offered and no call/fold; to_call > 0 => no check); assembly never repairs (R6).
R14: hand rankings and showdown (sheet p.2, p.5) are computed by core-engine::equity from the assembled cards; the model is never asked to rank or compare hands.

R15: unseated hero: hero_seat_index 'not_seated' at or above threshold (the low-confidence fallback does NOT count) AND action_on_hero confidently false AND ev_seat_controls confidently true => hero_cards [] (p1 not run), to_call 0, hero_chips 0, no Hero player, only p2 and p3_pot run, tier 2 skipped, players [].
R16: players for non-actionable states: 0.4.0 reads seat stacks (tier 2) but not bets, so a present seat can never be fully read: players is [] for every non-actionable state. Never a partial list.

R17: observation-only until calibrated: action_on_hero confidently true => evidence.readable=false and state null unless thresholds.calibrated is true AND every pass the actionable path uses (p1, p3_to_call, p3_hero_chips, p4_*) has calibration 'calibrated'. In 0.4.0 those passes are untrained_provisional, so no actionable state is ever produced.
R18: lobby-size guard: a frame whose size equals the calibrated lobby size never gets a table pass; a poker_table p0 answer then yields evidence.readable=false and state null.
R19: glyph segmentation contract: segmentation runs only in scripts/laya_prep.py (server and training share it). Rust never segments; it reads {n, overflow} from the server response.

questions.instructions: What kind of CoinPoker window is this?
Is a poker table with seats shown?
Are the player's own two face-up hole cards shown at the bottom seat?
Is the table's community-card area visible?
Is a pot amount shown on the table?
Are Fold / Check / Call / Bet / Raise action buttons shown?
Is a Find Seat or Join Wait List button, or an empty seat with a + button, shown?
Is the window content clearly visible (not covered or blank)?
Which betting round is shown?
Is it the player's own turn to act, with action buttons enabled?
Is a Fold button shown?
Is a Check button shown?
Is a Call button shown?
Is a Bet or Raise button shown?
Is an All-in button shown?
Which seat is the player's own seat?
